# TraceSQL: Traceable Answerability Estimation for Reference-Free Text-to-SQL Verification

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#tracesql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.17795v2) · arXiv:2608.17795v2, 24 August 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 14 pages, sections 1–11, supplementary A–F, all 67 feature definitions, tables 1–16, pipeline and rendered SHAP/correlation figures.

## Research question

A deployed verifier lacks reference SQL but needs to assess candidate correctness and expose the evidence behind its decision.

## Method

TraceSQL assembles LLM-produced ambiguity, planning, pair-analysis and intent-alignment evidence plus deterministic SQL-structure features. FLAML selects an Extra Trees classifier; 62 of the 67 input features survive preprocessing, with a fixed 0.5 decision threshold.

## Evaluation

Training uses 1,000 balanced positive/negative question pairs across 69 BIRD databases. External evaluation covers 1,521 generated candidates from 11 held-out databases; a separate all-positive reference-SQL test measures acceptance rather than two-class discrimination.

## What the results support

Aggregate generated-candidate F1/AUC improve over GradeSQL-7B, but reference-SQL acceptance is lower. Feature attributions expose influential signals and a false-positive example; they do not certify that the diagnostic explanations are correct.

## Limits and qualifications

Labels are reference-execution agreement on BIRD, not universal semantic correctness. The small classifier is lightweight, but feature production uses GPT-4o and GPT-5.2. Attribution is on development data and is not a causal feature-family ablation; ambiguity features are shared within positive/negative pairs.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A traceable candidate verifier rather than an input-unanswerability detector or a calibrated abstention guarantee.

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.
